route: scripted (procedural Blender geometry; no provider generation; face art reused from the P5-T6 UI atlas)

texturesSampled: ui/dice-d6 (shared UI atlas page, resident for the UI)
ui/dice-d6-glow (shared UI atlas glow page, the face emissive map)

lods: LOD0 only: a 40 mm die stays within the 1,500-triangle dice budget (DICE_LIMITS), so a LOD chain saves nothing measurable
bake: none: face art is the shared atlas page and brass is a factor (or the shared brass-polished set), so nothing is baked

frame.convention: src/dice/faces.ts die-local frame; identity orientation = DicePresenter's
frame.uv: TEXCOORD_0 is glTF (v down); loadDice flips v once so face UVs are in the UI atlas's bottom-left texture space

materialsUsed: factor-only polished brass named after the approved P4-T3 brass-polished set (bindable at runtime); the face slot samples the shared P5-T6 UI atlas page
license: Original work generated in Blender from a checked-in script; face art and style reference from Paul's paid Higgsfield plan (Terms of Use 4.4)

checks: face table (GLB extras and manifest) equals faces.ts and content/dice.ts
reimport gate (face-up UVs in the atlas cell, no mirrored UVs, Blender reimport)

approvals.notes: validate-generated-assets verdict is reported to the orchestrator, not self-recorded
original procedural geometry; face art from the P5-T6 atlas (its own provenance)
Paul approves the in-engine look (docs/blender-kit-project.md ruling 3)
blender-kit-pieces requires an independent >= 80/100 score; unscored means unaccepted

independentScore.scale: 0-100 visual fidelity to the art direction
independentScore.scorer: independent reviewer agent (separate from the authoring agent; did not build the asset)

rubric.note: Up 2 from 26. The v3 deduction, a pale grey-mauve inner wall (#847069, relL about 0.17), is resolved. On the right die the back wall at x=620, y 250 to 261 now measures #4E3E25 to #494039, relL 0.05 to 0.07, and the left wall scan at y=300 drops from the frame (0.35) to relL 0.006 to 0.02 within 2 px. On the lineup the top-face back walls measure relL 0.05 to 0.075 on dice x240, x400 and x560. The v3 low-saturation mask (S under 0.3, relL 0.10 to 0.35) still finds 4 to 294 px per lineup die, but these sit on the vertical brass frame edges (columns 290 to 300 on die x240, H33 to 39, relL 0.17 to 0.31), so they are desaturated brass highlights, not wall. The well now reads as panel 4's dark recess, and each pip has a dark lip (rim relL about 0.02). The frame is about 24 px of a roughly 330 px die (7.3% of die height) on the front-face side rail, with a rolled front lip that peaks at relL 0.90 (x=600, y 390). Points are lost because the wall stays a little above warm black (relL 0.05 against about 0.013, S down to 0.20) and the frame has flat slab faces rather than panel 4's softer pillowed bevel.

Up 2 from 19. The v3 pip-colour deduction is resolved. Pips measure #F3B554 (H37, S0.65, V0.95) on the right top face and #ECB354 to #EEB354 on the other faces, against candle amber #F3BE65 (H37, S0.58, V0.95), up from cream #E5C59B at S 0.32. The pip cup rim asked for in v3 now exists: around the right die's centre pip (centroid 606,307, 33 x 24 px) the ring at normalised radius 1.05 to 1.2 measures #3F250C, relL 0.024. Points are lost because the pips read as flat inlaid discs rather than lit lamps. Inside the disc relL runs only 0.53 to 0.55 from rim to core (core #F9B956, relL 0.555), while panel 4's pips grade from about 0.43 to a hot #FFF57F core at relL 0.88. The dark rim is the same in all eight octants (p10 relL 0.019 to 0.021), so it reads as an outline, not a cup with directional shading. The glow beyond the rim is weaker than in v3. The ring at radius 1.2 to 1.4 measures relL 0.096 against nearby walnut at 0.053 to 0.060, where v3 measured 0.125 against 0.066, and no pip light reaches the brass frame, which panel 4 shows clearly.

Up 1 from 12. The walnut grain is still painterly and strong. The well walls now read as shadowed wood, which removes the v3 note that the grey wall looked like a separate material. The brass is brighter and its range is wider. On the right die, hue-masked relL (S above 0.3) runs p10 0.223, p50 0.308, p90 0.427 and p99 0.614, against 0.117, 0.153, 0.235 and 0.68 in v3. The left die runs 0.238, 0.291, 0.389 and 0.607. The other half of v3 fix 3 is not met. There is still no edge wear or cavity darkening, so the brass is a smooth, even satin with high darks (p10 0.22) and few reflections. The top 5% of brass pixels go cream (#E3C38E, S 0.37) instead of staying gold, so it reads closer to painted metal or plastic than to panel 4's polished brass.

Up 2 from 10. The pips are now on palette (#F3B554 against #F3BE65). The walnut stays on target, with faces at #623D22, #53331E, #5F3A22 and #57351F and lineup faces at #56351E to #593A22, against #583C26. The off-palette grey-mauve wall (S 0.20) is gone. The brass moved toward the palette but is still short. The hue-masked median is #AD945D (H41, S0.46, V0.68, relL 0.31) on the right die and #A89057 on the left, against polished brass #DEC16A (H45, S0.52, V0.87, relL 0.55) and v3's #85692E (V 0.52). It reads as pale champagne or khaki gold at about 57% of the target luminance. The light frame, dark face and bright pip value structure is correct.

Unchanged at 9. Contrast did not rise, because the amber pips are slightly darker than the old cream ones. With v3's exact masks (pips relL above 0.45, walnut relL below 0.10) the closeup measures 5.53:1 and 6.27:1 on the right die's top and front and 5.62:1 and 6.13:1 on the left, against 5.55 to 6.15:1 in v3. On the lineup the v3 box-and-mask method gives 4.05 to 5.12:1, against v3's 4.75 to 5.90:1. That method's walnut sample now includes floor pixels (#714E36), so with floor-like pixels excluded the six lineup dice measure 5.43 to 5.83:1, and every die clears 4.5:1. The dark pip rim and the hue split between amber pips and brown walnut help segmentation. Downscaled by 0.55 so each die is about 78 px, close to the play-distance size, the pips on all six dice are still countable. A point is held back because contrast stays below panel 4, where the d6 pips (#F6B947, relL 0.55) measure 7.55:1 against the dark face pixels (relL below 0.06, #452916). The evidence is desktop only.

topFixes: Make the pips read as lit lamps, not flat discs. Inside the disc relL is flat at 0.53 to 0.55 (core #F9B956), while panel 4 grades to a hot #FFF57F core at about 0.88. Add a radial emissive gradient from a pale yellow-white core near #FFE89A to the current #F3B554 at the rim, and let the glow spill past the rim onto the walnut and the brass frame. The ring at radius 1.2 to 1.4 is only 0.096 against walnut at 0.055, and no pip light reaches the brass.

Polish the brass. The median is #AD945D (V 0.68, relL 0.31) against #DEC16A (relL 0.55), and highlights turn cream (#E3C38E, S 0.37). Lift the base colour or the probe response so the midtone nears #DEC16A, keep the highlights saturated gold, and add edge wear and cavity darkening so the darks fall from the current p10 of 0.22 toward 0.08.

Turn the uniform pip outline into cup occlusion. The rim measures p10 relL 0.019 to 0.021 in all eight octants. Shade the cup wall on the side away from the key light and leave the opposite lip lit, so the pips read as recessed cups instead of outlined stickers.

Darken the last of the well wall to warm black. The back wall is #4E3E25 to #494039 (relL 0.05 to 0.07, S down to 0.20) against #231D1A (about 0.013), which leaves a faint grey-brown band on the far side of each well.
independentScore.method: Independent reviewer (did not build the asset). I read the palette and dice sections of docs/art-bible.md and the references listed in assets-source/dice/<die>/provenance.json (L-board-1.png, panel 4, cropped at (60,956)-(750,1490), same crop as v3). I did not open any author self-score, status file, build note or commit message. Primary evidence was the shipped in-engine stills in the worktree, identified by md5 and mtime 2026-11-16 20:01 PST because git was off-limits: docs/verification/p5-dice-brass-d6.jpg (ad88fc95), p5-dice-brass-d6-lineup.jpg (7b7b80db), p5-dice-glass-d8.jpg (ad77e919) and p5-dice-glass-d8-lineup.jpg (fa4b9984), all 960x640, cropped and upscaled 2x to 4x for inspection. The renderer and GPU were not verified by me. The Blender renders and assets-source/dice/dice.review-sheet.jpg were used for shape only, because they render every surface through AgX. Measurements used Pillow and NumPy under python3 -I (scripts in /tmp/rxr-prev/dv4/tools): median sRGB in fixed boxes, hue-masked brass (H38 to 60 or 62, S above 0.3, cross-checked at S above 0.45), pixel scans across rails, frames and well walls, and ring or dilation-distance profiles around pips and numerals. Contrast ratios are WCAG (L1+0.05)/(L2+0.05) on relative luminance. Palette targets in relL: polished brass #DEC16A 0.55, candle amber #F3BE65 0.57, warm black #231D1A about 0.013. Play distance: a 40 mm die at about 0.7 m subtends about 3.3 degrees, roughly 80 px at Quest 3's roughly 25 px per degree. All evidence is desktop only, with no headset capture. Date 2026-11-16. For d6: pips were segmented at relL above 0.30 with H under 40 and S above 0.4 (v3's relL above 0.45 mask was rerun for comparison). Walnut was relL 0.01 to 0.12 with H8 to 35 and S above 0.35, excluding floor-like pixels where noted. Pip rings use ellipses normalised to the pip half-widths, and a lower-left pip profile was discarded because its window caught a second blob.
